summary.text: The bill would generally bar the government from using search warrants, subpoenas, court orders, and similar legal demands that could reasonably return records of Members of Congress or their staff, such as official written materials and electronic or wire communications. There would be exceptions, including when the person targeted is under criminal investigation, when the Member or staffer being investigated is the target, or when the records are certain electronic or wire communications. If such legal process is used under an exception and could or unexpectedly does return congressional records, the government would generally have to notify the Member or staffer and delay or halt reviewing the materials for 30 days. For certain records held by electronic or wire communications providers, a special master would have to be appointed to identify materials protected from disclosure under the Constitution.
